Christmas Glazed Ham

Served at: Christmas Day

Serves 10-12Prep 20 minCook 2 hours 30 min to 3 hours 30 min

A centerpiece of many Christmas feasts, a beautifully glazed ham brings a festive touch and savory-sweet flavor to the holiday table. This recipe features a classic brown sugar and mustard glaze, creating a caramelized crust that's both delicious and visually appealing, perfect for celebrating with family and friends.

Ingredients

  • 1 (8-10 pound) fully cooked bone-in or boneless ham
  • 1 cup (240 ml) packed light brown sugar
  • 1/2 cup (120 ml) Dijon mustard
  • 1/4 cup (60 ml) apple cider vinegar
  • 1/4 cup (60 ml) honey or maple syrup
  • 1 teaspoon ground cloves (optional)
  • Whole cloves for studding (optional)

Method

  1. Preheat your oven to 325°F (160°C).
  2. Remove the ham from its packaging and pat it dry with paper towels. Place the ham, fat-side up, in a large roasting pan.
  3. If desired, score the surface of the ham fat in a diamond pattern, about 1/4 inch (6 mm) deep. This allows the glaze to penetrate and creates a beautiful presentation.
  4. In a small bowl, whisk together the brown sugar, Dijon mustard, apple cider vinegar, honey (or maple syrup), and ground cloves until smooth.
  5. Bake the ham for 1 hour, then remove it from the oven.
  6. Brush about one-third of the glaze evenly over the entire surface of the ham. If using, insert whole cloves into the center of each diamond pattern.
  7. Return the ham to the oven and continue baking, basting with more glaze every 20-30 minutes, until the internal temperature reaches 140°F (60°C) for a fully cooked ham. This will typically take an additional 1 hour 30 minutes to 2 hours 30 minutes, depending on the ham's size.
  8. If the glaze starts to brown too quickly, loosely tent the ham with aluminum foil.
  9. Once the ham reaches the desired temperature, remove it from the oven, tent it with foil, and let it rest for 15-20 minutes before carving. This allows the juices to redistribute, ensuring a more tender and flavorful ham.
  10. Carve the ham against the grain and serve with any remaining pan drippings or extra glaze.

Tips

  • For a deeper flavor, add a splash of orange juice or bourbon to the glaze mixture.
  • Save the ham bone to make a delicious soup or broth later.
  • Leftover ham is fantastic in sandwiches, quiches, or diced into salads.
